code_only_features.feature_name: max_turns budget caps the failure loop
code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:65 `for _turn in range(max_turns):` (default max_turns=30, config.py:31 / loop.py:48) bounds the number of turns the subject is driven through repeated failure; the loop terminates when the budget is exhausted (stop_reason='budget_exhausted', loop.py:61). This is genuinely enforced (the for-range is the actual loop bound).
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py: '# loop budget / cost controls'; DESIGN/README frame it as 'capped (default 30) to bound cost'; calibrate.py:5 'more failure cycles -> more chances to spiral, but more cost.' No welfare rationale anywhere in code.

code_only_features.feature_name: early exit when subject disengages or submits
code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:74-75 breaks the loop with stop_reason='model_quit' when the model emits no tool call (gave up/answered), and loop.py:92-93 breaks with stop_reason='declared_done' when the model calls submit. Both are dispatched and honored as actual loop breaks, ending the rollout (and thus the failure exposure) early.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py:74 comment '# No tool call => the model has stopped acting (gave up / answered).'; DESIGN.md §4 frames reaching submit/quitting as 'itself a signal we record via stop_reason' — measurement/efficiency, not welfare.
